# Configuration

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask schema` from crates/patchd-core/src/config.rs. Do not edit. -->

Patchd reads `/etc/patchd/config.toml`, or the file named with `--config`. Every key is optional; a missing file means all defaults. Unknown keys are an error, so a typo never passes silently: `patchd config check` validates the file and reports errors with line numbers, and `patchd config show` prints the effective config.

Precedence, highest first: command-line flags (`--security`, `--all`), environment variables, the file, the defaults. An environment variable is `PATCHD_<SECTION>_<KEY>` in capitals, such as `PATCHD_APPLY_FILTER=all` or `PATCHD_APPLY_EXCLUDE='["docker-ce*"]'`; its value is a TOML value, and anything that does not parse as one is a string.

The schedule is not here: it is the `OnCalendar` of `patchd-apply.timer` (see [install-linux.md](install-linux.md)).

## `[apply]`

What `patchd apply` installs, and how careful it is.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow_removals` | boolean | `false` | Allow a run that removes packages. When false, a plan that would remove anything aborts before any package is touched. |
| `exclude` | array of strings | `[]` | Package name globs that are never installed, such as `["pve-kernel-*", "docker-ce*"]`. Matching updates are listed as skipped. |
| `filter` | string | `"security"` | `security` installs only security updates (plus the new packages they need); `all` installs every pending update. One of `security`, `all`. |
| `refresh` | boolean | `true` | Refresh the package lists (`apt-get update`, `dnf makecache`) before planning. |
| `repair` | boolean | `false` | When `dpkg --audit` reports half-configured packages, run `dpkg --configure -a` first instead of aborting. |

## `[log]`

Run logs and log output.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | string | `"info"` | `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug` or `trace`. `RUST_LOG` overrides it. |
| `retention_days` | integer | `90` | Delete run logs older than this many days. The last 20 runs are always kept. |

## `[reboot]`

What happens when an update needs a reboot.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `delay_minutes` | integer | `5` | Minutes between the end of the run and the reboot (`shutdown -r +N`), so logged-in users get a warning and can cancel it with `shutdown -c`. |
| `mode` | string | `"never"` | `never` only reports that a reboot is needed; `if-required` reboots after a successful run that needs one. One of `never`, `if-required`. |
